issues.description: The problem statement inconsistently refers to the animal feeding method as getFeedingSound() in several places, while the UML, the template, and the solution use the method name messageOnFeed(). This naming mismatch can confuse students about which method to implement and may lead them to implement getFeedingSound() instead of the intended messageOnFeed().
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across the problem statement and templates. Preferably update the problem statement occurrences of getFeedingSound() to messageOnFeed() (or, if getFeedingSound() is the intended name, update the template and solution to use getFeedingSound()). Ensure the UML, examples, and all textual references use the same method name so students clearly know which abstract method to implement.

issues.description: The problem description inconsistently refers to the animal feeding method with two different identifiers: the UML and method list use messageOnFeed(), while later textual instructions refer to getFeedingSound(). The reference to getFeedingSound() does not match the abstract method name implemented in the solution (messageOnFeed()) and may lead students to search for or implement getFeedingSound() instead of the intended messageOnFeed().
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier across all artifacts. Replace references to getFeedingSound() in problem_statement.md with messageOnFeed(), or alternatively update the template and solution to provide getFeedingSound() (possibly delegating to messageOnFeed()) so all materials use the same method name.
